answer: Trust propagates from independently anchored identities through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so a walk of fixed length assigns little mass to vertices rarely reached from honest sources. A sybil cluster with sparse external edges has low conductance; its quill-thin bridge to the honest graph limits escape and, by a conductance-based mixing bound, caps reachable sybil mass and thus aggregate voting weight. A large tundra of mutually attesting accounts cannot evade that cut merely by adding internal edges.
